supporting_observations.claim: At 14:16:09 UTC, explorer.exe running as ivy.chen updated a UserAssist value whose ROT13-decoded name references Windows PowerShell. This is a PowerShell-related artifact, but the record does not identify a command, script, parent process, or execution time corresponding to the reported 13:40 window.
Around the reported time, proxy records show ivy.chen requesting the Salesforce login page and its web resources. These records do not establish what caused the reported PowerShell window.

At 13:45:05 UTC, the proxy recorded a successful tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent and approximately 38.8 MB received. This is consistent with update-related traffic, but does not establish that authorized patching caused the reported PowerShell window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status metadata states that both Sysmon and Windows Security logs from WS-ICHEN-01 were not collected between 13:30 and 14:10 UTC, encompassing the reported 13:40 activity. This metadata has no record ID.
The available network records around 13:40 show web requests but do not provide PowerShell command lines or process ancestry (T054-00140, T054-00141, T054-00142).
The later UserAssist registry record contains binary data without decoded usage details; it cannot independently timestamp or characterize the reported execution (T054-00356).
claims_not_established: Whether the reported PowerShell window executed a malicious command, an authorized maintenance script, or another benign action.
Whether sam.okafor initiated remote patching from WS-SOKAFOR-01 using the approved Apply-Updates.ps1 script.
Whether the PowerShell-related UserAssist artifact at 14:16 corresponds to the reported 13:40 activity (T054-00356).
Whether any network connection, persistence change, credential access, or data transfer was caused by the reported PowerShell activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Attempt recovery of locally retained Windows Security, Sysmon, and PowerShell Operational logs from WS-ICHEN-01 for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including process creation and script-block records.
Obtain remote-management and process records from WS-SOKAFOR-01, plus relevant FILE-NWD-01 script-share access records, to test the authorized-patching explanation.
Ask sam.okafor to confirm whether maintenance targeted WS-ICHEN-01 around 13:40 UTC and provide the executed command, script version, and job records.
Collect and decode the relevant UserAssist entry and obtain available PowerShell history or other execution artifacts to clarify the significance of T054-00356.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: WS-ICHEN-01 established a proxy tunnel to desktop.dropbox.com with a DropboxUpdate user agent at 13:26:57 UTC. Dropbox is outside the supplied approved-services inventory; this record does not establish file upload or a relationship to the PowerShell report (T054-00062).

Separate ticket: GlobalProtect PanGPA.exe launched as ivy.chen at 13:29, and Cisco AnyConnect vpnagent.exe launched as SYSTEM at 14:18. These warrant inventory review given the supplied no-VPN context, but the records do not establish an active VPN connection or a relationship to the reported PowerShell activity (T054-00069, T054-00072, T054-00372, T054-00373).
